CoverMap v0.6.2 · July 2026 · FEASIBILITY DEMONSTRATOR · IML 2 · illustrative data · not clinical guidance

CoverMap Nigeria — the right antivenom, pre-positioned

Nigeria carries the largest snakebite burden in West Africa; the Middle Belt (Kaltungo, Gombe, Benue) is the carpet-viper epicentre. Which WHO-assessed antivenom to place at which hospitals, how many vials, and how much of the burden it brings within reach.
85.5%of the carpet-viper burden brought within reach of the right antivenom (from ~0%), via 63 hospitals
~19,541carpet-viper envenomings/yr the plan brings within reach (of 22,865 nationally)
36,671vials/yr demand forecast (~$2,931,101/yr procurement)
1.5%of burden beyond 50 km of ANY hospital — the structural gap stocking alone can't close (shown, not hidden)

Nigeria's modelled scale is ~9× Ghana's — the same method, a far larger burden. Because Nigeria is hospital-dense, only 1.5% of burden is beyond reach of any hospital (vs 6.2% in Ghana).

Nigeria's absolute figures are the least anchored in this project — stated plainly. No published per-eco-zone snakebite rate exists for Nigeria. The zone rates are a construction, not a transcription; an earlier version described them as "facility-anchored and calibrated", which overstated their provenance. They sit between two published bounds: FMoH surveillance recorded ~15,278 cases/yr (7.6/100,000, certainly under-reported), while community surveys in savanna foci report ~497/100,000. Our implied facility attendance (21.6/100,000) is ~2.8× the surveillance figure, which assumes substantial under-reporting — plausible, but assumed. The implied envenoming rate (14.0/100,000) falls inside the published West-Africa range (8.9–93.3/100,000, Habib 2013, J Venom Anim Toxins Trop Dis 19:27 (West Africa 8.9-93.3/100k/yr)) — a bound, not a confirmation.

Unresolved uncertainty we could not settle: the strongest Nigerian community datum (~497/100,000) is attributed to the Benue valley by Habib, but the underlying 1980 study is generally sited at Malumfashi (Katsina) — i.e. it may belong to the Sudan savanna, which we rate lower than the Middle Belt. If so, the gradient between our two savanna zones could be inverted. Both zones are high and both are prioritised, so the placement conclusion holds; the split between them is not established.

The plan on the map

The decision it changes — quantified

A. Status quo — product that FAILS Echis (Bharat/Indian polyvalent)0.0%0~0 (0–0)$0
B. Naive — good product only at 48 tertiary/central hospitals20.4%4,657~480 (289–559)$698,511
C. Optimized — PANAF-Premium at 63 hospitals85.5%19,541~2,013 (1,212–2,345)$2,931,106
D. Structural ceiling — good product at all hospitals98.5%22,511~2,319 (1,396–2,640 †)$3,376,612

† Upper bound capped at 2,640 — the highest published estimate of Nigeria's total annual snakebite mortality (GBD 2019 UI upper). Antivenom-preventable deaths cannot exceed total deaths, so we cap the figure and say so rather than print an arithmetically-derived but impossible number. The cap binds only in the theoretical all-hospital ceiling scenario, not in the recommended plan.

What's at stake — and where our own number strains. The tool's direct, defensible output is coverage: 85.5% of the carpet-viper burden brought within reach of an effective antivenom. The deaths column applies the observed Ghanaian product-choice differential (case-fatality 1.8% → 12.1% under a failing product, Visser 2008) to the patients the plan reaches — an extrapolation from Ghana to Nigeria. Nigeria loses an estimated 1,460–1,927 people/year to snakebite in total (GBD 2019 1,460, UI 977–2,640; Habib 2015 1,927, 1,529–2,333).

We flag rather than tune: our central figure (2,013) exceeds the highest published CENTRAL estimate of Nigeria's total snakebite mortality (1,927). It stays under the highest published upper bound (2,640), and it is a worst-case counterfactual rather than an expectation — but it should be read as an upper-bound signal, not a forecast, and it is the clearest evidence that Nigeria's absolute figures carry wider uncertainty than Ghana's. This is why the headline is coverage and vials, never a deaths count. Placement is robust: 52/63 hospitals stay chosen under a flattened gradient.

From decision to action: demand per hospital

Who the plan covers

Limits, by design. Subnational stock is unobservable → we model placement choices, not measured inventory. Access is straight-line ≤50 km, a proxy for travel time. Zone rates are a CONSTRUCTION with no published per-zone source, bracketed by FMoH surveillance below and community surveys above; urban LGAs inherit their zone's rate, which overstates their snakebite burden. The envenoming fraction (64.7%) is transferred from northern Ghana (Aglanu 2025) and is assumed for Nigeria. No care-seeking multiplier is applied: in the facility frame these patients have already reached care (an earlier version double-counted it, understating the vial forecast). Population is afripop's within-country distribution scaled to the national total (206.1 M, World Bank 2020) — the raster's own absolute counts are not used. 2 facility names carrying a duplicated suffix in the upstream Maina/WHO file were repaired (suffix only; no facility renamed). Not clinical guidance.
The urban artifact, quantified — and why it doesn't change the plan. Because urban LGAs inherit their eco-zone's rural rate, the model's single highest-burden unit is Municipal Area Council (Abuja Federal Capital Territory) at ~757 envenomings/yr — about 7.8× the 95th percentile. That is an artifact, not a finding: snakebite envenoming is overwhelmingly rural. We show it rather than hide it, and we quantify its consequence: it dominates the map's colour scale, but only 1.2% of the planned vials go to the FCT or Lagos, and every top-priority hospital sits in a savanna or Middle-Belt state (Kano, Niger, Kaduna, Gombe, Jigawa, Katsina, Kogi, Benue). The decision is robust to the artifact — which is precisely why we report the placement, not the raw burden raster.

Parameter provenance — what is sourced and what is not

Every load-bearing number was taken back to primary sources. "Not confirmed" below means searched hard, no published figure exists — not "unchecked". Nigeria carries more unconfirmed parameters than the other demonstrators, and they are the reason its absolute figures should be read as indicative.

ParameterStatusBasis
Echis fraction 0.85 (savanna)SourcedHabib & Abubakar 2011 (Kaltungo, 6,687 victims): ">90% of the bites were due to E. ocellatus"; Habib 2013 series 75%

Mortality differential 10.3 ppPartialVisser 2008 — observed, but measured in Ghana; transferring it to Nigeria is an extrapolation
Envenoming fraction 0.647PartialAglanu 2025, measured in northern Ghana; assumed for Nigeria
Reach 50 kmPartial — proxypublished standard is 3 h travel time (Longbottom 2018); the distance conversion is ours
Price $80/vialPartialpublished prices span $3.4–$315; $120/course sits inside the $100–153/dose modelling baseline
Zone rates 45 / 28 / 4Not confirmedno published per-eco-zone rate exists for Nigeria at any resolution. A construction bracketed by FMoH surveillance below and community surveys above. Drives every absolute figure here.

CoverMap v0.6.2 · July 2026 — v0.6.2 — separates DEMONSTRATED FAILURE from ABSENCE OF DATA in the coverage matrix. PANAF-Premium x Naja katiensis was rendering as partial cover while its own cell recorded a measured failure (Khochare 2024, 11.16 LD50/mL, below the 20 threshold); four untested Atractaspis cells were rendering in the same red as documented failures, asserting more than the evidence supports. Failure now overrides every higher grade and is visually distinct from no-claim and no-data. Also corrects six stale figures in the methods page and adds publish.py, which diffs generated output against the published site instead of copying by hand. v0.6.1 — corrects three Ghana figure titles that still displayed 87.5%, the pre-v0.4 coverage value, while every text KPI on the same page said 86.0%; the numbers are now read from the model JSON and a fifth verification suite OCRs every shipped figure to keep image and text in agreement. v0.6 added the targeting-scenario table for India and a parameter-provenance table to all three briefs. v0.5 confirmed 4 of 10 assumed parameters against primary sources and labelled the remaining 6 NOT CONFIRMED. v0.4 corrected the care-seeking double discount and India's state death rates.

Same West-African coverage matrix and recommended product (PANAF-Premium — WHO risk-benefit-assessed, broad, heat-stable/lyophilised) as the Ghana demonstrator. Real inputs: 774 LGAs (geoBoundaries, CC BY 4.0); population WorldPop/afripop2020 distribution (CC BY 4.0) → 206.1 M (World Bank 2020); 1,309 hospitals (Maina 2019 Sci Data 6:134 / WHO). Impact anchored to Habib 2015 PLoS NTD 9(1):e0003381; national mortality GBD 2019 (Nat Commun 2022) and Habib 2015 PLoS NTD 9(9):e0004088; incidence range Habib 2013 J Venom Anim Toxins 19:27. Illustrative feasibility demonstrator — not clinical guidance.
